IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
Writ Petition (S/B) No.639 of 2026
30th September, 2026
Jai Kumar -----Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others ----Respondents
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Deputy Advocate General along with
Mr. M.S. Bisht, learned Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
-----------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta C. J.)
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The present writ petition has been filed assailing
the transfer order dated 24.09.2026 and the
consequential relieving order dated 25.09.2026 issued by
the respondent authorities whereby the petitioner, who is
presently serving as Professor in the Department of
Physiology, Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali (VCSG)
Government Institute of Medical Sciences & Research,
Srinagar Garhwal has been transferred to Government
Medical College Haldwani.
3. The main ground on which the transfer order
has been challenged is that the petitioner was appointed
and posted at the present place of posting on 13.05.2025
1

and within a short time of one year he has been
transferred. It is contended that the same is contrary to
the provisions of the Transfer Act, 2017.
4. Learned State Counsel has placed on record the
instructions received from the Director of Medical
Education, Uttarakhand. Paragraph nos.4 and 6 of the
instructions, which are relevant, are as follows:
"4. That in the present writ petition, the petitioner has
primarily challenged the transfer order No 1340/XXVIII
(5)/2026 (E-31073) dated 24.09.2026 passed by the
office of Medical Health & Medical Education
Department, Govt. of Uttarakhand, specifically
mentioning that "the change of postings was directed to
be implemented immediately". It is submitted that the
transfer of the faculties/ staff is a policy matter of Govt.
of Uttarakhand, which is time-to-time implemented
considering the priority of patient welfare and the
academic functioning of the Institutes. Moreover, the
petitioner is not alone to be transferred instead many
other faculties were also transferred to meet the NMC
requirement of different State Medical Colleges for safe
guarding the academic interest of the students.
5......
6. That it is relevant to mention in the present context
that a PIL (no 202/2026) has also raised the concerns
about transferring faculties from Haldwani. Moreover,
MD physiology course is running in department of
Physiology in Haldwani Medical College and there is no
professor available, therefore in the interest of
academics it is necessary to transfer the faculty."
5. As the petitioner has been transferred to meet
the NMC requirements and to fill up the vacant post of
Professor in Haldwani Medical College in the Department
of Physiology, therefore, we are not inclined to interfere
with the transfer order.
2

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further
submitted that the impugned transfer order is mala fide as
the petitioner had earlier filed two writ petitions and,
according to him, it is on account of the said reason that
he has been transferred. However, as noted above, the
transfer has been made to fill up the vacant post of
Professor in the Department of Physiology and to meet the
NMC requirements. Therefore, the contention that the
transfer order is mala fide has no merits and cannot be
accepted.
7. The petitioner holds a transferrable post and
transfer having been made in public interest, there is no
occasion for this Court to interfere with the transfer order.
8. The writ petition lacks merit and the same is,
accordingly, dismissed.
9. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed
of accordingly.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
